text: Starr Andrews, born on June 23, 2001, in Los Angeles, California, is an American figure skater who was home-schooled and has a brother and two sisters, including Skylar, a gymnast, and Ashton, a baseball player. Her mother, Toshawa Andrews, suffers from cardiac microvascular disease, which has resulted in a dozen heart attacks. Andrews became interested in figure skating when her mother took her to an ice rink at age three, and she began learning to skate in 2005. A video of nine-year-old Andrews skating to "Whip My Hair" went viral on YouTube in December 2010 and reached 53 million views by March 2018. Derrick Delmore became her coach around 2013, and she placed sixth on the novice level at the 2016 U.S. Championships. She moved up to the junior level under Delmore and Peter Kongkasem in Lakewood and Riverside, California, and won the junior ladies title at the Golden Bear of Zagreb in October 2016. She earned a junior silver medal at the 2017 U.S. Championships and was added to the U.S. team for the 2017 World Junior Championships in Taipei, where she finished twelfth after placing ninth in the short program. Beginning her junior season, she placed fifth at the ISU Junior Grand Prix in Austria and made her senior international debut at the 2017 CS Golden Spin of Zagreb, where she placed sixth and achieved the minimum technical scores for senior-level ISU Championships. In 2018, she finished sixth at the U.S. Championships, placing eighth in the short program and fifth in the free skate, and competed at the Four Continents and World Junior Championships (withdrawing from the latter and being replaced by Emmy Ma). At the 2018 CS Asian Open, she placed second in the short program but dropped to fifth after the free skate; at the 2018 CS Autumn Classic International, she ranked fifth in the short and seventh overall, attempting a triple Axel that was downgraded due to insufficient rotation. She made her Grand Prix debut at the 2018 Skate America, placing ninth in the short program, tenth in the free skate, and tenth overall, and later competed at the 2018 Skate Canada International, where she placed fourth in the short program, ninth in the free skate, and seventh overall. She finished eighth at the 2019 U.S. Championships, won silver at the 2019 International Challenge Cup and the 2019 Egna Spring Trophy, and placed fifth at both the 2019 CS Lombardia Trophy and CS Finlandia Trophy. At the 2019 Internationaux de France, she placed fourth in the short program and fifth overall in the free skate. She finished sixth at the 2020 U.S. Championships and eighth at the 2020 World Junior Championships. In 2020, she competed in a virtual U.S. domestic event, placing fourth, and at the 2020 Skate America in Las Vegas, she placed eighth. At the 2021 U.S. Championships in Las Vegas, she placed twelfth. She placed fifth at the 2021 CS Autumn Classic International and was named to replace Bradie Tennell at the 2021 Skate America, where she placed tenth; she also finished fifth at the 2021 CS Cup of Austria and withdrew from the 2021 Internationaux de France due to injury. At the 2022 U.S. Championships, she placed ninth, earning a spot at the 2022 Four Continents Championships, where she finished ninth. She underwent surgery for supraventricular tachycardia, a condition she had experienced for nearly a decade. She placed sixth at the 2022 CS Nebelhorn Trophy and finished fifth in the short program at the 2022 Skate Canada International before "surprising" many by winning silver in the free skate, becoming the first Black American woman to win a Grand Prix medal in singles since the 1995 era and the second Black woman after Surya Bonaly. She noted the significance, saying it was a huge deal for her as one of the few people of color in the sport. At the 2022 NHK Trophy, she planned to add a second flip to her free skate after recovering from an ankle "tweak," but dropped to ninth after the free skate when she did not execute the planned flip. At the 2023 U.S. Championships, she placed third in the short program, made two jump errors in the free skate, and was overtaken for bronze by Amber Glenn, but still won a pewter medal and stood on the senior podium for the first time, becoming the first African-American woman to do so since Debi Thomas in 1988. She had her preparation delayed due to a planned Coachella appearance that did not happen and later underwent heart surgery for atrial tachycardia, a condition she had managed for a decade. She began working on her programs by July and debuted at the Kings Cup International in early October, winning silver. At the 2023 Skate Canada International, she finished sixth in the short program and eighth overall due to jump problems in the free skate; she placed tenth at the 2023 Grand Prix of Espoo. At the 2023 CS Golden Spin of Zagreb, she won the bronze medal. At the 2024 U.S. Championships, she placed ninth in the short program but delivered a strong fifth-place free skate, moving up to sixth overall. She began the 2024–25 ISU Challenger Series with fifth at the Cranberry Cup International and tenth at the Denis Ten Memorial Challenge, won silver at the 2025 Pacific Coast Sectional Championships, qualifying for the U.S. Championships, and won gold at the 2024 Santa Claus Cup. At the 2025 U.S. Championships, she placed twelfth in the short program but fifth in the free skate, finishing sixth overall, and closed the season with a fourth-place finish at the 2025 International Challenge Cup. She recorded the vocals for the track "Turning Page" used in her free skate. Beginning the 2025–26 Challenger Series, she placed seventh at the 2025 CS Nepela Memorial and twelfth at the 2025 CS Trialeti Trophy. In November, she announced that the 2025–26 season would be her last as a singles skater and that she would switch to pair skating beginning with the 2026–27 season. Selected as a host pick for 2025 Skate America, she delivered two clean programs, earning a new personal best free skate and combined total score, placing fifth overall, and also finished fifth at the 2025 CS Tallinn Trophy. At the 2026 U.S. Championships in January, she finished seventh and was named to the 2026 Four Continents team.
